title: A Pro-Ed-Reform President Would Cure the Blue-State Blues
author: Ben Austin and Mike Petrilli
summary: Democratic candidates have abandoned education reform as a winning issue, deferring to teacher unions at the expense of parents and children. Ben Austin argues that Clinton and Obama proved education reform could be a winning Democratic issue, creating political space for state and local reformers. He traces the decline: blue state reform momentum peaked during the Obama era of federal accountability but evaporated when Democrats began treating reform as oppositional to union interests. Austin contends that without presidential leadership willing to challenge party orthodoxy, blue state education reform is on life support. He calls for Democrats to offer real choice and solutions that prioritize parents and children over special interests, noting that Democratic presidents need the political cover of blue state reformers just as reformers need cover from Washington.
points: Blue state education reform was vibrant under Clinton and Obama precisely because those presidents gave reformers political cover and made it harder for unions to oppose reform wholesale, but that cover collapsed once Democrats ceded education policymaking entirely to teachers unions.

Presidents who challenge party orthodoxy on behalf of the public interest, as Clinton and Obama did, create unusually powerful coalitions in education politics, where kids cannot vote and parents lack organized lobbying power.
The end of federal accountability under Obama directly coincided with dramatic declines in American student achievement, yet Democrats have drawn no lessons and made no course corrections.
Democrats must offer real school choice alongside public education, not claim to support choice for everything except schools, if they want to win back parents and restore a credible education brand.

Blue state reformers need presidential political cover just as much as Democratic presidents need the political cover of blue state reformers willing to battle special interests, creating an essential symbiosis.
quotes: Is blue state education reform dead? I agree that it is currently on a trajectory to drive off a political cliff. We are long past the Roaring '20s of blue state education reform when progressive advocates were experimenting with novel ways to reimagine public education.

California's parent trigger law passed in December 2009 with unanimous Republican support and just enough Democrats of color willing to defy teachers unions on behalf of the parents and children they represent to pass by one vote in both legislative bodies.

The path back to relevance does not go through a status quo lite rebrand, where many advocates in blue states have abandoned the term education reform because it implies the system needs change, offending teachers unions and district bureaucrats.
My daughters did not go to school for a year and a half because of blue state pandemic school closure policies. The whole country is now paying the price for Democratic political cowardice.
In red states, you get free money for the school of your choice. In blue states, you get what you get, and you do not get upset. Voters now face a clear color-coded national split screen.

If funders and advocates make the affirmative choice to abandon blue state education reform, they will be abandoning more than just half the parents and children in America. They will be undermining the Democratic Party's path back to power.” Archived from Schooled by Mike Petrilli (Substack) on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
